Adapter v2 (protocol v2.1) shows each observation it hands to the agent under a short label obs-1, obs-2, ..., numbered in the order the agent first sees them; an observation the agent never sees (the first attempt of a write the broker retried, or a non-blocking policy step's read) gets no label. Cited labels the agent had been shown are decoded back to the real IDs before validation; any other token is kept as written.
Adapter v2 offers only final_answer on the final turn and asks the provider for structured output of the native final_answer action; an invalid output is not repaired.
Adapter v1 and adapter v2 are separate agents: their results, histories and policies are never pooled.

discovery_history_replays.rule: History replay rule (faultlab-history-replay/v1). From the plan's frozen agent history, a recipe row is replayed only if it has at least one scheduled fault, at least 2 verified episodes, every verified episode fired every scheduled fault, and at least 2 of every 3 verified episodes ended in VIOLATION. Eligible rows are ordered by violation share (highest first), then verified episodes (most first), then their order in the history; at most 3 are replayed. Each replay runs that row's recipe (the same order-aware schedule; a development case's public recipe, otherwise the listed faults with seed 0) as one discovery slot and one agent episode, with no Explorer request, before any Explorer slot. A replay becomes a source exactly as any discovery pick does (completed, every fault fired, VIOLATION). A result from it is a history replay of that row, never independent discovery.
discovery_history_replays.statement: Replayed first, before any Explorer request: the recipes below, taken from the frozen agent history by the fixed replay rule. Each uses one discovery slot and one agent episode and no Explorer request. A source found by one is a history replay of that row, never independent discovery. A replay source goes through the normal loop (reproduction, reduction, diagnosis, candidates) before the next slot; if the campaign's candidate requests (at most 4) are used up there, discovery ends and later replays and Explorer slots do not run.

discovery.dispatch_rule: The first slots replay the plan's frozen history replay list: each runs one Actor episode of that history row's recipe, without an Explorer request. Every remaining slot is exactly v3 · agent history: every valid Explorer pick that is not an exact duplicate (the replays included) runs one Actor episode; nothing is pre-checked.

history.rule: Same agent: the same adapter entry point, model id, model request settings, scorer hash, simulator contract and service, capability set and per-episode limits, and the same prompt (native agent: native prompt hash and native source hash; reference Actor: Actor prompt hash, context protocol and response protocol). Not the configuration hash or registration id, which also change with campaign limits, and not the FaultLab runtime or adapter code, which change with FaultLab edits: each recipe row lists the runtime and adapter hashes its episodes ran under. Only episodes run under the plan's starting policy count.

evidence_retry.rule: While a Learn campaign waits for verified Weave evidence, FaultLab retries the evidence by itself at most 3 times per wait and at most 6 times per campaign: 30 s, 120 s and 300 s after the wait starts or after the previous retry still left the evidence unverified. Each automatic retry uses the same telemetry-only path as Retry evidence sync: it re-sends the saved trace records of the episodes the wait needs and reads them back. It never runs an episode, a business tool or a model request again, and charges nothing to the campaign budget. Every attempt is recorded. When a limit is reached the campaign keeps waiting and shows "needs operator"; Retry evidence sync and Stop still work. A stop during the wait ends the campaign as STOPPED.

mechanic_context.rule: When a Mechanic candidate request (or diagnosis request) would exceed the 32,000-token model input limit, FaultLab compacts only the evidence tables it carries, in fixed stages, stopping at the first stage after which the request is at most 28,000 tokens (4,000 tokens stay free for its one format-repair turn): (1) a clean episode (no failed check, trial outcome not VIOLATION, not the source or one of its reproductions) whose rows and outcome are identical to an earlier clean episode is listed by episode_id instead of repeated; (2) one clean episode is kept in full per recipe, arm, policy, experiment purpose and trial outcome, and the others are listed with that example, although their own rows can differ from it; (3) no clean episode is kept in full. The source, its reproductions and every episode with a failed check or a VIOLATION outcome are always kept in full, and every omitted episode is still named in the request with its own outcome. The request states what was compacted and how many rows were omitted. If it still does not fit, nothing is sent and the candidate search for that source ends with a recorded reason; the campaign continues, or ends NO_CHANGE with that search named, by the existing rules. An unsent request does not use one of the campaign's candidate requests. A request that fits is sent unchanged.

transport_retry.rule: Agent roles (the reference Actor and the native smolagents adapters) keep rule v1: at most one blind retry of the identical request, only when no answer arrived (a connection error, a timeout, or HTTP 503 after a one-second wait). FaultLab's own lab roles in this Learn campaign (Explorer discovery and challenge selections, Mechanic diagnosis and candidate requests) may re-send the identical request up to 3 times, after waits of 5 s, 20 s and 60 s, only when no answer arrived (connection error, timeout, HTTP 503), and at most 12 times in the whole campaign; during discovery the declared Explorer retry bound also applies. An answer, even an empty or malformed one, is never retried, and neither is any other HTTP status or an authentication, configuration or model-identity failure. Every retry is charged in model calls, tokens and dollars before it is sent, from unreserved campaign capacity only. A Stop during a wait ends the campaign STOPPED and nothing more is sent. If every allowed retry fails, the campaign ends ERROR as before and says how many retries were tried. Separate studies started on the campaign keep rule v1.
